name: Freelance graphic designer (contests and 1-to-1 projects)
summary: Apply to join 99designs as a designer, then compete in client design contests or take paid 1-to-1 projects such as logos and branding.
what_you_do: Once accepted, you either enter contests, where many designers submit concepts for one client brief (logo, packaging, social graphics) and only the chosen winner is paid, or you work directly with clients on 1-to-1 projects at a price you set. Your Entry, Mid or Top level controls which contests you can enter and the fee you pay.
who_it_may_fit: You already have solid design skills and a portfolio and can afford to do unpaid contest entries while building a reputation.
Free to sign up, and clients come to the platform, so you do less self-marketing than going solo
Platform fees fall as you move up levels: 15% at Entry, 10% at Mid and 5% at Top on 1-to-1 projects
A way to build a portfolio and client relationships that can continue as 1-to-1 work
who_it_may_not_fit: You're new to design, need dependable income, or object to doing unpaid speculative work.
Contests are speculative: losing entries aren't paid, and a study of about 38,000 contests found a large share of designers never win a single contest
One paid winner can face hundreds of other entries (TechCrunch)
Acceptance is competitive. A curation team reviews applications, and after two declined attempts you are declined permanently
Entry-level designers can only enter the lower-priced Bronze and Silver contest packages (third-party summary)
Fees: a 15–5% platform fee depending on level, plus a $100 introduction fee for each new client, spread over that client's first $500
Payouts go only through Hyperwallet since January 2026
A March 2026 Trustpilot reviewer said most of the entries they received were AI-generated (anecdotal). 99designs says it has systems to catch rule-breaking designs
Job Bank rates the 2025–2027 outlook for graphic designers and illustrators as Very limited in Ontario, so competition for design work is high
No source names Canada as an eligible designer country. Eligibility is inferred from the platform's worldwide designer base

conditions_notes: Contest income depends on winning against many entrants. Academic study of about 38,000 contests: a few designers win consistently and many never win.
No platform training found. Professional design-software skills and a strong portfolio are expected.

fees: Platform fee on 1-to-1 projects: 15% (Entry), 10% (Mid) or 5% (Top level). A $100 introduction fee per new client, spread over that client's first $500 in charges. Free to sign up.
economics_notes: No official designer earnings figures found. Third-party sites list client logo-contest prices from US$249 (Bronze) to US$1,050 (Platinum); one critical review estimates the winner receives roughly 60% of the contest fee (unverified). 1-to-1 project prices are set by the designer.

name: Stock photo, video & illustration contributor
summary: Sell licences to your photos, videos, vectors and illustrations through Adobe Stock and earn a share of each sale.
what_you_do: You create and upload images, footage or vector art with titles and keywords through the Adobe Stock Contributor portal. Submissions are moderated, and accepted files earn a royalty whenever an Adobe Stock customer licenses them.
who_it_may_fit: You already create photos, video or vector art and want to earn a little from a growing back catalogue over time.
Free to join with an Adobe ID. Adobe says there are no upfront or subscription fees
Adobe's published royalty rate is 33% for photos, vectors and illustrations and 35% for video
Adobe sets per-download royalty floors for large-subscription sales (about $0.33–$0.38, rising with lifetime licences)
Payouts through PayPal, Payoneer or Skrill
who_it_may_not_fit: You need predictable income soon or don't want your earnings to depend on an algorithm and a crowded library.
Per-download earnings are often under $1. Adobe's own example is about US$0.99 per photo on a 10-licence monthly plan, and as low as $0.33–$0.40 on large plans
You can only request a payout once you have at least US$25 and 45 days have passed since your first sale

Contributors on Adobe's forum report sharp download drops in 2025–2026 (one went from 50–60 to 10–20 a week with 6,200+ assets). Community experts blame competition from AI-generated content, now about half the library (anecdotal)
Forum posters also complain of vague rejections and some account deactivations. Adobe staff don't answer individual account issues on the forum
Without a valid US tax form, Adobe withholds tax at the maximum rate (30%)
Your country of residence is fixed when you create the Adobe ID
You must be 18 or older

conditions_notes: Income depends on buyer downloads. Adobe community forum threads (2025–2026, anecdotal) report large, unexplained drops in downloads and blame a growing share of AI content.
No required training; must follow Adobe's account, content submission and model-release guidelines.

economics_notes: Official: royalty 33% (photos, vectors, illustrations) and 35% (video) of the net licence price, based on the US purchase price. Adobe's contributor page shows about $3.30 per download on a small monthly plan, down to $0.33–$0.40 on the largest plans; extended and HD/4K licences pay more. Free-collection placements pay a one-time credit instead. Payout minimum US$25. No typical monthly income is published.

name: Film & TV production assistant (category)
summary: Entry-level crew work on film, TV and commercial sets, sometimes reached through short crew-training programs. Job Bank files production assistants under NOC 53111.
what_you_do: Production assistants (PAs) support crews on set and on location: running errands, helping move and set up equipment, managing people and traffic around the set, distributing paperwork and helping whichever department needs a hand. The work is on-site, usually by the day or by production, and long days are common.
who_it_may_fit: You like fast-paced, physical teamwork on location and can handle long days at short notice.
A recognized way into Canada's screen industry that usually doesn't need a degree
Job Bank says the occupation usually requires a college diploma, an apprenticeship of under 2 years, or more than 6 months of on-the-job training
Free or low-cost crew-training programs have run in Toronto, Northern Ontario and B.C., some aimed at youth from under-represented groups
Toronto's earlier PA training program was recognized by the Directors Guild of Canada – Ontario toward its apprenticeship program, which cut the entry cost by 75% (City of Toronto, 2019)
who_it_may_not_fit: You need remote work, regular hours or steady weekly income.
Job Bank's 2025–2027 outlook is Very limited in Ontario and in the Montréal/Laval and Montérégie regions, Limited in Kitchener–Waterloo–Barrie and Moderate in Nova Scotia
Job Bank 'production assistant' wages ($16.00 low, $24.94 median, $36.49 high per hour) were last updated November 2023
Job Bank says these workers usually work more than 40 hours per week. Long, irregular days are typical
Work comes one production at a time, so income is irregular and depends on local filming activity
The training programs found (Toronto, Northern Ontario, B.C.) come from 2019–2023 reporting. No 2026 intake was confirmed
On-site only, not remote

requirements.education: College diploma, apprenticeship under 2 years, or 6+ months on-the-job training usually expected (Job Bank)

conditions_notes: Project-based on-set work. Job Bank estimates about 2,200 workers in NOC 53111 in Ontario, with a Very limited outlook there for 2025–2027.
Some crew-training routes have been free (e.g. Northern Ontario crew training sessions, Reel Canada workshops); none confirmed running in 2026.

advertised_rate.note: Job Bank 'Production Assistant' Canada wages, last updated 29 Nov 2023: $16.00 low, $24.94 median, $36.49 high per hour. An undated Playback article reported PA day rates of $125–$150 at two Toronto commercial production companies (likely old). Current rates not verified.

name: Stock photo, video & illustration contributor
summary: Upload your photos, video clips or illustrations to Shutterstock's library and earn a percentage each time a customer licenses one.
what_you_do: You shoot or create images, footage or vectors, add titles and keywords, and submit them for review. Approved files stay in the library and earn a royalty each time they're downloaded, so income builds slowly and depends on a large portfolio of subjects buyers want.
who_it_may_fit: You already take good photos or videos or make illustrations and want a low-effort side outlet, without counting on the money.
Free to join, and you work whenever you like
Uses skills and gear you may already have (camera, phone, design software)
Approved files can keep earning for a long time without new effort
Earnings levels go up from 15% to 40% of the sale as your downloads grow within a year
who_it_may_not_fit: You need predictable income soon; most contributors earn little per file and sales are slow.
Earnings per download are small: Shutterstock pays 15% to 40% of the sale depending on your level, and some downloads pay only the $0.10 minimum
Levels reset to Level 1 every January 1, so even busy contributors drop back to the lowest rate each year
The 2020 switch to this percentage model cut typical subscription-download pay sharply and caused contributor backlash (Amateur Photographer, Fstoppers)
Contributors report more files earning fewer sales as libraries grow and AI images compete (contributor blog, 2026)
Non-US contributors need an approved W-8BEN tax form before being paid. Without a treaty rate, 30% can be withheld on licences bought by US customers
Trustpilot reviewers (2025, anecdotal) describe accounts closed with earnings held. Shutterstock says closing an account that still has a balance can take up to 90 days
You must be 18 or older

conditions_notes: Income depends on buyer downloads, not hours worked. Contributor blogs and journalism describe falling per-file returns since 2020 and growing AI competition.
No required training; contributors must follow Shutterstock's content submission guidelines.

economics_notes: Official help centre: 6 earnings levels each for images and video, from 15% to 40% of the sale, reset to Level 1 on 1 January; some downloads pay the $0.10 minimum (currency not stated in indexed text). 2020 coverage listed thresholds of up to 100 downloads (15%) through 25,001+ (40%); current thresholds not confirmed. Monthly payouts by the 15th once a minimum payout amount is reached (one third-party blog says $35, unverified). No typical income figure is published; treat as small, irregular side income.

name: Social media coordinator / community manager (category)
summary: Planning, posting and monitoring social media content for an organization, as an employee or freelancer. Job Bank files it under professional occupations in advertising, marketing and public relations (NOC 11202).
what_you_do: You plan and schedule posts, write captions, prepare simple graphics or short clips, answer comments and messages, and report on engagement. Employees usually sit in a marketing or communications team. Freelancers manage accounts for several small businesses or creators.
who_it_may_fit: You write well, enjoy online communities and simple visuals, and can show results through a portfolio.
Job Bank national wages for social media coordinators: $20.50 low, $35.58 median, $57.44 high per hour (updated November 2025)
Job Bank's Alberta page says 21% of this occupational group is self-employed, against 15% across all occupations, so freelance work is common
Yukon outlook is rated Good for 2025–2027, partly because businesses increasingly rely on social media and digital platforms (Job Bank)
Much of the work can be done remotely and in writing
Related titles to search include marketing coordinator, media coordinator and digital marketing consultant (Job Bank)
who_it_may_not_fit: You want work with no audience or client contact, or need a steady paycheque soon without a degree or portfolio.
Job Bank says the occupation usually requires a university degree. Without one, entry generally relies on a portfolio and freelance or volunteer results
No national outlook was found. Alberta and Nova Scotia are rated only Moderate for 2025–2027 (Job Bank)
Job Bank says workers in this group usually work more than 40 hours per week

Fake 'social media' jobs are a major scam. The Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre warns of 'task' offers to like, boost or review products, apps or videos that pay small amounts and then demand deposits. Reported losses were $49M in 2024 and $46.5M in the first nine months of 2025
A legitimate social media job never asks you to pay, buy crypto or 'unlock' tasks
Freelance work has no guaranteed hours or benefits

requirements.education: University degree usually required for employee roles (Job Bank)

conditions_notes: Employee roles are ordinary salaried jobs. Freelance volume depends on building a client base. Outlook varies by province: Good in Yukon, Moderate in Alberta and Nova Scotia (2025–2027).
No specific training requirement found beyond the university degree Job Bank says employee roles usually expect.

name: Video, audio & podcast editing (category)
summary: Editing video and audio, from short social clips to podcasts, as an employee or freelancer. Job Bank groups video and sound editors with audio and video recording technicians (NOC 52113).
what_you_do: You cut raw footage or recordings into finished pieces: trimming, sequencing, adding captions, music and graphics, cleaning up sound and exporting for each platform. Freelancers often turn long videos or podcasts into short clips for social media. Employees work for production companies, broadcasters, recording studios and post-production houses.
who_it_may_fit: You like detailed, creative computer work and can teach yourself editing tools and build a sample reel.
Job Bank lists a national median of about $30/hour for videotape editors (NOC 52113), with a range of about $20–$46
Project-based work, much of which can be done remotely
Skills carry over to social media, captioning and podcast production, so one skill set serves several kinds of clients
Film editors (NOC 51120) have a higher Job Bank median of about $38.94/hour, showing a progression route
who_it_may_not_fit: You need steady hours right away or can't invest in a capable computer and software.
Job Bank wage figures for videotape editors were last updated November 2023 and may be dated
Job Bank's 2025–2027 outlook for NOC 52113 is Limited in most regions and Very limited in Ontario and Montréal
Job Bank says employee roles usually need a college diploma or 2+ years of apprenticeship. Film editor roles usually need a university degree
Podcast producer jobs found asked for a lot of experience (one Scotiabank posting required 5+ years of podcast, broadcast or similar production)
You need a capable computer and editing software. Their cost was not researched
Freelance demand is irregular, with no guaranteed volume

requirements.education: College diploma or 2+ year apprenticeship usually expected for employee roles (Job Bank)

conditions_notes: Job Bank outlook for NOC 52113 (2025–2027): Limited in most regions, Very limited in Ontario and Montréal, Moderate in Centre-du-Québec. Few openings expected from retirements. Freelance volume depends on clients.
Job Bank: employee roles usually expect a college program (e.g. recording engineering or audiovisual technology) or apprenticeship. Freelancers often self-teach; course costs not researched.

name: Young Canada Works student jobs in heritage
summary: Federally funded summer and student jobs at museums, archives, libraries and heritage sites for students aged 16–30. You apply to employers through the Young Canada Works portal.
what_you_do: Depending on the employer, you might guide tours, help with collections and archives, run programs and events, or support an organization's outreach. Positions generally last 6 to 16 weeks at 30–40 hours a week. A separate internship stream, Building Careers in Heritage, serves college and university graduates.
who_it_may_fit: You're a student aged 16–30 (citizen, PR or refugee status) interested in museums, archives, arts or history who wants paid summer experience.
Paid work experience in the arts, culture and heritage sector, which can be hard to break into
Employers set pay. One museum's 2026 postings, funded through YCW or Canada Summer Jobs, paid $18.25/hour for 30 hours a week
Students have no application deadline and apply through one national portal
A graduate stream offers longer internships after college or university
who_it_may_not_fit: You're not a student, are over 30, hold a temporary visa, or need year-round or remote work.
Only for Canadian citizens, permanent residents or people with refugee status. International students and temporary-visa holders are excluded
You must be 16–30 and enrolled in high school, college, CEGEP or university (heritage student stream)
Short-term: usually 6–16 weeks, mainly in summer
Employers do the hiring. The program doesn't place you
The Canadian Museums Association warned a House of Commons committee of a funding cliff that could eliminate 600+ youth jobs, so there may be fewer positions
On-site work at the heritage organization

requirements.education: Current enrolment in high school, college, CEGEP or university (student stream); Valid social insurance number

conditions_notes: Fixed-term placements of 6–16 consecutive weeks at 30–40 h/week (CMA). How many positions exist each year depends on federal funding, which the CMA warned is at risk.
No program-level training requirement found; employers train students on the job.

economics_notes: Wages are set by employers ('competitive for the region', per the Canadian Museums Association). Example: one heritage employer's 2026 postings funded through YCW or Canada Summer Jobs paid $18.25/hour for 30 h/week. Not a program-wide rate.
